context.description: The task-ui classifies every unit only from the status tags

evidence.trustReason: The decoded eleven-task status supplies harness class tags for waiting, active phase, trusted, dead, blocked and cancelled tasks. The real Board render asserts every column, card order and heading count. STOPPED assertions put dead before blocked before cancelled in both Board and shared list. Counts, focus and next-running assertions exercise store selectors and actor selection. Renamed and contradictory state values prove classifications use tags; the active phase alone uses DISPLAY for its phase column. The source scan detects state-name lists and ACTIVE/ENDED identifiers, while inspected store and Board code keep the single state-keyed DISPLAY table for presentation.

context.gherkin:
Scenario: UI1 The task-ui classifies every unit only from the status tags
    Given a status with waiting, active, trusted, dead, blocked and cancelled tasks
    When the Board and the counts read it
    Then waiting tasks are in WAITING, active tasks in the column of their phase, stopped tasks in STOPPED and the other ended tasks in TRUSTED
    And STOPPED groups dead tasks, then blocked tasks, then the rest
    And the counts, the focus and the next running task come from the tags
    And the task-ui keeps no list of active or ended state names
